$comment: Concord-authored additions to FedRAMP 2026 KSIs. Keyed by 2026 indicator ID.
FedRAMP authors the statement, name and control mappings
(fedramp-consolidated-rules.json); Concord authors only what is here.
rules: still empty. No phase-one rule is carried onto a 2026 indicator, and
a verdict rule is added only after reading that indicator's own statement.
methods: Concord platform posture checks curated per KSI (ccf.fedramp20x.methods).
The bar: the check's FAILURE must contradict the indicator's statement.
Sharing a mapped 800-53 control is not enough. A failing method raises the
KSI to warn; a passing one is evidence; neither makes it pass, because most
2026 KSIs describe a practice persistently reviewed, which configuration
cannot prove. Each rationale quotes the words the failure contradicts.
Revised after independent review against each evaluator's code: a check
that can FAIL while the statement is met (it reads too little, or fails on
unrelated data shapes) is not a method, however relevant its title sounds.

methods.rationale: Fails when SMS, voice or email is an enabled authentication method; an interceptable factor contradicts "phishing-resistant MFA".
Fails when the AWS root user has no MFA device; the most privileged account signing in by password alone contradicts "strong passwords with phishing-resistant MFA".
Fails when ordinary accounts can create tenants, register applications or create security groups; that is access beyond "only access the resources they need".
Fails when any member can invite external guests; granting outsiders access is not limited to "the resources they need".

Fails when an enabled account has been inactive over 90 days; an unused account keeps access it does not "need". (A break-glass account kept deliberately idle will trip it; record that as an exception.)

Fails when every ordinary account holds standing rights to create tenants, register applications or create security groups; standing privilege contradicts "least-privileged ... authorization model ... for all user ... accounts".
Fails when an enabled account has been inactive over 90 days; it was not disabled, contradicting "the lifecycle ... of all accounts ... securely managed".
Fails when no directory audit record exists in the last 7 days; directory changes are not being recorded, contradicting "Modifications ... are logged".
Fails when no multi-region CloudTrail trail is logging; AWS API changes are not recorded, contradicting "Modifications ... are logged".
Fails when no multi-region trail is logging; AWS activity reaches no central log, contradicting "centralized ... logging of events, activities, and changes".
Fails when no sign-in audit record exists in the last 7 days; sign-in events are not being logged, contradicting "to ensure these activities occur".
Fails when no directory audit record exists in the last 7 days; directory change events are not being logged, contradicting "to ensure these activities occur".
Fails when no multi-region trail is logging; AWS API events are not being logged, contradicting "to ensure these activities occur".
Fails when a bucket has no default server-side encryption rule; objects written without one are stored unencrypted, contradicting "Information is encrypted or otherwise secured".
Fails when a storage account accepts plain HTTP or TLS below 1.2; data in transit to it is not "secured from unwanted access or modification".
Fails when a database instance has PubliclyAccessible set; its data is exposed to the internet, contradicting "secured from unwanted access".
Fails when an active IAM access key is older than 90 days; a key that old was not rotated, contradicting "regular rotation of digital keys ... is automated".
Fails when a node's latest Puppet run failed; automation is present but not converging, so that node's configuration is not "managed using automation".
Fails when a node has not reported in 24 hours; its configuration is neither managed nor "persistently reviewed for drift".
Fails when a node's latest Puppet run failed; its intended state is not being applied, contradicting "automatically enforce their intended operational state".
Fails when a node has not reported in 24 hours; it is not being assessed, contradicting "persistently assess the security of all machine-based information resources".
Fails when a security group allows SSH or RDP from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0; inbound administrative traffic is unrestricted, contradicting "configured to limit inbound ... network traffic".
Fails when a database instance has PubliclyAccessible set; inbound internet traffic to it is not limited, contradicting "limit inbound ... network traffic".
Fails when SSH or RDP is open to the internet; an exposed administrative port contradicts "a minimal attack surface".
Fails when a database instance has PubliclyAccessible set; an internet-facing database contradicts "a minimal attack surface".
